feature: A drawing says which component it is while you look at it
summary: Point at a copy of a component, or pick it, and the mark above it spells out the component's name. Let go and it goes back to the bare mark, so three Save buttons in a row still read as three quiet buttons rather than three labels all saying Save button.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next, Components on. Draw a box, Layer > Make Component, name it Save button.

try.do: Put three copies of the component on the canvas from the Library shelf.
Look at the row: each copy wears one small violet diamond and no words.
Rest the pointer on the middle copy. It says Save button above itself.
Move the pointer off it. The words go, the diamond stays.
Click the last copy. It says Save button and keeps saying it.
On the original, press Add beside Versions and name a second version Disabled.
Rest the pointer on the first drawing of that pair: it says Save button · Default.
Move the pointer off it: it goes back to saying just Default.

evaluate: Pointing at a copy to learn its name: is that where your hand already is, or would you rather the name were always printed?
The name arrives on a small dark plate while every resting label is plain violet text. Does the plate read as a temporary answer, or as a tooltip that does not belong on the canvas?
Only ONE drawing spells its name out at a time, and pointing at something beats having picked something. Does the picked one losing its words while you point elsewhere read as correct or as a glitch?

A picked copy says its name in violet; a picked original says it in the selection blue, because only the original's word answers a click. Does that colour difference tell you anything, or does it just look inconsistent?

Two copies of one component that show different versions read Save button · Default and Save button · Disabled when you point at each. Is the version worth the extra width there, or is the name enough?
rough: A copy nobody is pointing at still says nothing, and that is the deliberate part. Printing the name on every copy is what the 2026-09-08 version-labels work removed: a screen built out of twelve buttons wears twelve identical labels, each wider than the button under it, and the row climbs into a staircase. So the name came back as something you summon rather than something you read. If you want it printed on every copy anyway, that is a real answer and this is the line to disagree with.

Where the labels sit is still worked out from what they say AT REST, so the one you are looking at can reach over a neighbour's mark. It draws last and on a plate so it is always the legible one, but it can cover a neighbour's short word while you point.
Double clicking a spelled-out original still renames the VERSION, so a label reading Save button · Disabled opens a field holding just Disabled. Filed as a follow-up.

Panning or pinching now re-reads what the pointer is on, so a name does not go on hanging over a drawing that slid away. Switching tools from the keyboard without moving the pointer still leaves the name up until the next mouse move; the hover tint has always behaved that way.
Both screenshots are real screen captures: the probe held the Screen Recording grant for these runs.
